A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FUSE research work, with readable text, equations, tables and figures. v1 ends after its references; v2 includes an additional 11-page supplement. All supplied material was included in the comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original shape-matching experiments, embedding and diffusion comparisons, SDF and volumetric evaluations, and qualitative application results.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds baseline comparisons, robustness experiments, smoothness analyses, runtime measurements and anchor/solver evaluations.

M1.justification: The conditional-flow objective, independent per-shape flows, shared-anchor composition and nearest-neighbor retrieval remain unchanged. v2 adds a tested spectral-smoothing preprocessing variant for WKS and pretrained embeddings (supplement Equation 11; Tables 2 and 9), constituting a limited procedural extension.

E1.justification: The datasets, representation types and downstream tasks are retained, including cross-representation matching already described in v1. v2 adds evaluation with perturbed landmark locations (Figure 4), extending coverage to noisy landmark inputs.

E2.justification: v2 adds evaluated Diff3F and ULRSSM comparisons, including Diff3F with functional maps in Table 4. It also includes FUSE_DDIM in the main benchmark comparison, beyond the dedicated diffusion comparison retained from v1. KNN-IN-GAUSS becomes FUSE_ANCHOR; that renaming is not an added baseline.

E3.justification: v1's 45-pair embedding comparison is replaced by FAUST/SMAL comparisons with different descriptor dimensions and Euclidean-error/feature-energy reporting. v2 introduces controlled landmark, smoothing, anchor and solver settings. Its supplement also specifies SHREC20 evaluation on remaining common points after selecting six input landmarks, refining v1's stated common-landmark evaluation.

E4.justification: v2 adds landmark perturbation/count studies, controlled embedding-smoothness experiments, smoothing of pretrained features, alternative-anchor tests and solver accuracy/runtime analyses (Figure 4; supplement Figures 14–15 and Tables 9–11). These substantially expand the questions tested beyond v1's embedding and FM-versus-DDIM comparisons.

E5.justification: v2 adds per-pair metric distributions with medians, interquartile ranges and outliers across four benchmarks (Figure 13), supplementing v1's averages. This reports variability across shape pairs; neither PDF establishes repeated-seed uncertainty estimates, confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: v2 replaces embedding results and adds extensive baseline, cross-representation, robustness and computational results. SHREC20 FUSE Euclidean error changes from 0.0846 to 0.0975; the revised evaluation description prevents interpreting this as an established same-setting regression. Newly evaluated ULRSSM leads FAUST/SMAL accuracy in Table 4. Existing SDF and volumetric table values are retained.

T1.justification: v2 adds a theorem-based argument about coincident flows for identical embedding distributions and independence from training couplings (Section 4.2). Supplement Section 1.2 adds mathematical reasoning contrasting finite-time FM anchoring with asymptotic DDIM anchoring. The core objective and composition equations remain unchanged.

C1.justification: v2 narrows 'first neural representation' to 'first flow-matching based representation,' replaces the zero-shot framing with composition requiring no further optimization and shared landmarks, and frames competitive accuracy around landmark-based matching. The central contribution of composing flows for correspondence across representations is retained.

C2.justification: v2 substantially expands the interpretation of embedding failures through smoothness and frequency, explains landmark priors, and explicitly identifies partial matching and non-bijective nearest-neighbor retrieval as limitations. The supplement adds explanations of inversion deviations and anchor instability. v1 mainly discusses map smoothness and unreliable point-cloud geodesics.

D1.justification: v2 discloses the six-layer, 256-dimensional MLP, Fourier encoding, training budget, hardware, memory/time requirements, baseline implementations, spectral settings, metric normalization and ground-truth landmark transfer. These details are absent from v1. v2 also supplies a code link, although its supplement retains future-release wording; actual availability is not established by the PDFs.

R1.justification: v2 adds targeted discussion of template-based methods such as 3D-CODED, FARM and NICP, revises the optimal-transport discussion, and adds references supporting smoothing, implementation and partial-matching directions. It narrows the novelty positioning while retaining the central relationship to flow matching, Geometry Distributions and functional maps.

P1.justification: The flow rationale, embedding-selection discussion and conclusion undergo substantial rewriting. Dataset descriptions are redistributed between the main text and a structured supplement, terminology is standardized, and the narrative is reorganized around prior assumptions, robustness and limitations. These changes extend beyond adding experimental content.

P2.justification: v2 changes the document from two-column to single-column layout, redraws the overview and application diagrams, expands the embedding and benchmark tables, and adds robustness curves, distribution plots and supplementary comparison tables. Several existing figures and tables are retained with relocation or relabeling.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially addresses v1's missing implementation information and limited examination of failure conditions. Stronger comparisons, controlled robustness/smoothness studies and explicit limitations make the work more reproducible and its claims easier to assess. Some bijectivity and exact-anchoring statements remain inconsistent with the added qualifications, but these residual issues do not outweigh the substantial gains in evidence and transparency.
